reference: 2019 landings; retained catch universe includes zero labels.
method: Independent simple trophic chain using saved taxon coefficients; 51 source ecological groups.
confidence_note: Overall confidence is the weaker membership or allocation confidence. Each rule percentage is its share of independent simple-chain PPR.
missing_note: 100 labels lack a saved TL/coefficient. All have zero recorded2019 landings, so each contributes zero annual PPR and the reference total is complete. Coefficients themselves remain unavailable.
unresolved_note: No unresolved mappings remain; high mapping coverage includes explicitly assumed broad categories and analogues.
source_limit: The source reports juvenile catches as zero and has no discard observations. Those zeros supply a historical catch-composition proxy, not evidence that target discards or later catches contain no juveniles.

rule_names.M1: Explicit species assignment in the source composition table
rule_names.M2: Verified synonym of an explicitly listed source species
rule_names.M3: Unambiguous fit to the documented residual cephalopod group
rule_names.M4: Supported extension from listed regional representatives
rule_names.M5: Supported ecological extension to a documented guild
rule_names.M9: Assumed eligible group set supported by source taxonomy and ecology
rule_names.M10: Broad reporting category approximated across compatible groups
rule_names.M11: Closest represented analogue despite habitat or taxonomic mismatch
rule_names.W1: One eligible group; no allocation split needed
rule_names.W4: Source-model1991 reported catch proportions, assumed across target years and bases
rule_names.W9: Model-biomass proportions when complete candidate catches have zero total

very_low_decisions.reason: Broad ray-finned-fish reporting spans named fish, pelagic, coastal and shelf pools. Approximate with source fish pools3–29 except11/20 (selacians), which are taxonomically excluded. Constituent composition is unobserved.
Bathypelagic or oceanic midwater fish lack their own depth/feeding compartment. Pelagic L is the closest mobile pelagic-fish analogue, with deep-water/feeding differences retained.

Oceanic, highly migratory or large filter-feeding elasmobranch lacks a matching pool. Shelf selacians is the closest offshore cartilaginous-fish analogue; oceanic/depth or feeding differences (especially basking shark/mobula) are material. Coastal selacians would not resolve those differences.
Deep slope fish exceed the modeled shelf domain. Shelf L includes a deep-associated macrourid and provides a meaningful predatory demersal-fish analogue, with depth/composition mismatch retained.

Deep/slope large crustaceans extend beyond the modeled <200 m shelf and lack a deep-water pool; shelf large crustaceans are the closest represented benthic decapod analogue. This habitat mismatch is retained.

Broad shark reporting spans source coastal/shelf habitats and potentially oceanic/deep species. Both selacian pools are a meaningful approximation; no observed species/habitat composition supports stronger containment.

Deep-water dogfish/shark assemblage extends beyond the modeled shelf. Shelf selacians (including Squalus/Oxynotus/Galeus) is the closest taxonomic/demersal analogue, with depth and unlisted-species mismatch.
Chimaeras have no source group and differ taxonomically from selacians; shelf selacians are the closest cartilaginous demersal-fish analogue, with deep-water and feeding mismatch.
Broad cartilaginous-fish label includes sharks/rays in both source pools and potentially unrepresented chimaeras. Approximate with both meaningful selacian pools; disclose unrepresented component.

Broad decapod reporting can include large harvested shrimps/crabs/lobsters and smaller benthic forms. Use large and small Banc/shelf crustacean pools; cannot infer strict large-only containment from provider commercial tag. Exclude pelagic macrozooplankton because source macro examples are euphausiids/mysids rather than harvested adult Decapoda.

Pelagic/rafting goose barnacles are crustaceans without a matching sessile-epifaunal compartment. Small benthic crustacean pools are the closest size/taxonomic analogue, with habitat and feeding mismatch.

Composition unspecified across large and small benthic crustaceans and macrozooplankton (euphausiids/mysids). Retain those compatible compartments; source catch labels do not establish a complete size/habitat boundary. Meio/larval pools excluded as not a plausible adult fishery reporting population.
Unidentified finfish can span named fish, pelagic, coastal and shelf pools. No observed composition supports a narrower exclusion; approximate with all source fish pools (3–29), including selacians.

Groundfish reporting establishes demersal tendency but no species mix. Include compatible named and generic coastal/shelf fish groups, including demersal elasmobranchs; exclude strictly pelagic/mullet pools.

Pelagic reporting spans migratory mullets, the five named pelagic pools, Coastal M (Ethmalosa), Shelf M (explicit pelagic/benthopelagic jacks) and offshore selacian analogue (potential pelagic sharks/rays). Pool names do not exclude these known exceptions. Unobserved composition is a broad approximation; strictly benthic fish pools are excluded.

Unidentified invertebrate reporting can include cephalopods, large/small crustaceans, molluscs, worms, echinoderms and other macro-invertebrates. The provider tag is not exhaustive; named and residual compatible macrofaunal pools retained. Meio/mesoplankton and primary producers excluded as unsupported harvested reporting components.

The taxonomic label can include cephalopods and benthic molluscs. Provider demersal-invertebrate tag does not prove cephalopods absent. Retain both named cephalopod groups and Banc/shelf mollusc pools in a broad composition approximation.
Mesopelagic lanternfish are not a represented source fish pool. Sardinelles/anchovy supplies the closest small schooling zooplanktivorous-fish analogue, despite depth and diel-migration mismatch.
Broad order includes benthic octopuses represented by Octopus vulgaris and potentially pelagic argonaut/octopod forms in other cephalopods; unobserved composition is approximated across both.

Historical broad perch-like reporting spans many source fish pools. Approximate using compatible named/guild compartments, excluding clupeiforms, selacians, catfish and flatfish-only groups; no observed constituent mix is available.
